subject.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values

question: What value may `openclaw config validate` disclose in the new `got:` hint when authored config, includes, SecretRefs, and environment-resolved effective values differ?
rationale: The accurate value is the post-resolution value that failed validation, but printing it can expose secrets or private configuration; source inspection alone cannot choose that product and security contract.

options.title: Provenance-gated effective values
options.body: Show the effective rejected scalar only when its provenance is known and the path/value passes conservative sensitivity checks; otherwise omit the hint.

options.title: Authored values only
options.body: Show only the literal value from the source file and document that `got:` may differ from the effective value used for validation.

options.title: Omit received values
options.body: Land line numbers and bracket notation while dropping `got:` hints to preserve the existing disclosure boundary.

recommendation.title: Provenance-gated effective values
recommendation.body: Show the effective rejected scalar only when its provenance is known and the path/value passes conservative sensitivity checks; otherwise omit the hint.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent config I/O and effective-runtime configuration work makes this the closest available owner for choosing the parsed-versus-resolved diagnostic boundary.
